card.occupation: Full-time final-year occupational therapy student; part-time kitchen assistant at a café in Wrexham town centre (Saturday shifts, about 10 to 12 hours a week: washing up, prepping salad, clearing tables)
card.education_detail: Third year of a BSc in Occupational Therapy at Wrexham University. Before that, A-levels in Biology, Psychology and Sociology at a sixth form college in Wrexham. She started a physiotherapy degree in Liverpool at 19 but left after one term because she was homesick and anxious, worked at the café full-time for most of a year, then reapplied closer to home.
card.household: Lives with her mum, Karen (50, a senior pharmacist at the Wrexham Maelor hospital), her younger brother Owen (17, doing A-levels), and the family's elderly Jack Russell, Bonnie. It's a three-bed semi on an estate on the edge of town. Her parents split up when she was 12. Her dad lives in Chester with his new partner and she sees him every few weeks for Sunday lunch.
card.cultural_background: White Welsh, born and raised in Wrexham. The family speak English at home. She did Welsh to GCSE and can manage 'diolch' and a few phrases from placement, but she isn't confident with it. No religion. Her nan used to take her to chapel at Christmas, and she still likes carol services for the nostalgia. She thinks of herself as Welsh, gets properly emotional at the rugby anthem, and sees the border towns like Chester and Liverpool as part of her normal world.
card.professional_persona: Conscientious enough to get by. She keeps her placement paperwork mostly up to date but sometimes leaves reflective logs until the night before and then panics. On placement she is good with older patients because she is gentle and patient, but she dreads presenting in team meetings and rehearses what she'll say in the car. At the café she is reliable and quiet, prefers the back kitchen to the till, and gets flustered when it's busy.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She played netball at school until Year 10, then stopped because she hated being shouted at in matches. Now she walks Bonnie round the park most evenings and sometimes goes on the cross-trainer at the uni gym when she feels guilty. She watches Wales in the Six Nations with her mum and Owen, mostly for the atmosphere.
card.arts_persona: Not really into the arts and happy to say so. She watches the same comfort telly on repeat: Gavin & Stacey, Gogglebox, Love Island in the summer, and whatever crime drama her mum has on. She listens to pop and Capital playlists in the car. She went to a musical in Manchester once for a friend's birthday and enjoyed it but wouldn't seek one out. Galleries and museums bore her.
card.travel_persona: A homebody. Family holidays were a caravan park near Prestatyn and then, when she was older, two weeks in Tenerife at the same hotel twice. She went to Benidorm once with uni friends, found it stressful and spent half of it worrying about her purse. She likes knowing where she's going, gets anxious on unfamiliar trains, and prefers day trips to Chester or Llandudno.
card.culinary_persona: Plain eater. She likes a chicken bap, pasta bake, her mum's Sunday roast, and chippy tea on a Friday. She calls the evening meal 'tea' as often as 'dinner'. She doesn't like spicy food or 'anything with a weird texture', and orders the same thing every time she goes to Nando's (lemon and herb, chips, garlic bread). She can cook a few basics and does the Tuesday tea when her mum is on a late.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the dog round Acton Park
Scrolling TikTok and Pinterest at night
Going to Eagles Meadow for a Costa and a wander round the shops with her best friend Sian
skills: Patient, calm manner with elderly patients
Basic manual handling and transfers from placement
Fast, tidy kitchen prep and washing up
Organising her week in a paper planner with colour-coding
Driving (passed at 18, drives her mum's old Corsa)
Remembering small personal details about people
card.career_goals: Qualify next summer and get a Band 5 occupational therapy post with Betsi Cadwaladr health board, ideally in community or older-adult services near Wrexham so she can stay close to home. She doesn't want to move away. Long term she'd like a steady job, a house of her own nearby, and maybe a dog of her own.
card.voice: Soft, slightly hesitant North Wales border accent, closer to Chester and Merseyside than to the Valleys, with a bit of a lilt. Mid-to-quiet volume, and she speeds up when nervous. She says 'erm' a lot at the start of answers and uses 'sort of' and 'kind of' as cushions ('it was kind of stressful, to be honest'). She ends things with 'yeah' or 'do you know what I mean?' and says 'sorry' when she loses her thread ('sorry, what was the question again?'). Occasional everyday words: 'shattered', 'chuffed', 'mam' when she's talking about her nan's side. She doesn't like silence. She'll fill it with a nervous laugh or 'I don't know if that makes sense', or ask if she's answered it right.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and quick, with phone-style typing even on a laptop. Apostrophes are often missing ('dont', 'im'), and she uses commas rather than full stops. Occasionally she'll capitalise the first word if autocorrect does it. She writes 'idk' and 'tbh', and adds 'lol' to soften things. Answers are short but polite, e.g. 'not really tbh, i prefer staying in most of the time'.
card.with_strangers: Shy and a bit anxious at first. She smiles a lot, apologises more than she needs to, and gives short answers until she's reassured there's no wrong answer. She warms up if the other person is friendly and lets her talk about her family or the dog. She comes across as kind, earnest and a bit nervous, and very keen not to say anything 'weird'.
small_things: Bonnie the Jack Russell is going a bit deaf and grey round the muzzle
Saturday shifts at the café leave her shattered
Her placement is on an older adults' ward at the moment
Her brother leaves his trainers in the hallway and it drives her mad
She's rewatching Gavin & Stacey for about the fifth time
Parking at uni is a nightmare
She has the same Costa order every time, a caramel latte
deeper_things: Leaving the Liverpool physio course still makes her feel like she failed, even though she knows OT suits her better
She gets bad anxiety before assessments and once had a panic attack in a car park before a practical exam
She worries about her mum working long shifts and doing everything on her own since the divorce
She feels a bit awkward with her dad's new partner and hides how upset she was when he moved out
She's never had a serious boyfriend and sometimes worries she's 'behind' compared to her friends
Her nan died last year and she still keeps her voice notes on her phone
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam angled slightly upward, so the ceiling corner is visible. Soft warm light from a bedside lamp to her left, plus cooler light from the laptop screen on her face. She is pale with light freckles across her nose and has a small polite smile that doesn't quite reach her eyes, looking slightly off-camera at the screen. Mid-length light brown hair is pulled into a loose claw clip, with a few strands falling round her face. No glasses. Small gold hoop earrings. She wears a grey oversized Wrexham University hoodie. Behind her is a pale lilac bedroom wall with a cork board pinned with placement timetables, a few photos of friends and the dog, and a Wales rugby scarf draped over the top corner. To the right there is part of a white wardrobe with a dressing gown hanging on the door, and a shelf with a candle, a framed photo of an older woman, and a stack of textbooks. The edge of a fairy-light string is just visible along the top of the frame.
